name: Crow Island School
by: Perkins, Wheeler & Will with Eliel and Eero Saarinen
features: One-storey wings off a shared core; every classroom has its own outdoor court, under a tall chimney tower.
note: Only two files in the category; the first shows the entrance and brick chimney tower, partly behind trees.

name: Baldwin Hills Village (Village Green)
by: Reginald D. Johnson; Wilson, Merrill & Alexander; Clarence S. Stein
features: A car-free superblock: low garden apartments face large shared greens, with garages kept to courts at the edge.
note: The photo seen shows the central green with low houses at its edges: the defining space rather than one facade.

name: Equitable Building (Commonwealth Building)
features: Early glass-box tower: first clad in aluminium, double-glazed, sealed and fully air-conditioned.
note: Now called the Commonwealth Building; 14 storeys. Many photos in the category.

name: Price Tower
features: Wright's only built skyscraper: floors cantilever like branches from a central core, with copper louvres.

File:Price Tower, Dewey Avenue, Bartlesville, OK - 53707616527.jpg

note: Category also has HABS measured drawings: Category:Price Tower, 510 South Dewey Avenue, Bartlesville, OK - HABS drawings (public domain), useful as extras.

name: General Motors Technical Center
by: Eero Saarinen and Associates with Smith, Hinchman & Grylls
features: A campus of long steel-and-glass blocks with glazed-brick end walls in bright colours, around a lake and a dome.

photos.file: File:General Motors Technical Center, Warren, Michigan LCCN2011633194.tif
File:General Motors Technical Center Building, Warren, Michigan LCCN2011631234.tif
File:General Motors Technical Center, Warren, Michigan LCCN2011631554.tif
File:General Motors Technical Center Mound Entrance.JPG

note: Best photos are Carol Highsmith's public-domain Library of Congress TIFFs (the styling dome; a blue glazed-brick end wall). File:Warren - General Motors Technical Center (50826111923).jpg shows a newer blue building, not Saarinen's: don't use it.

name: Deere & Company Administrative Center
features: Office floors wrapped in a frame of weathering steel and deep sunshades, spanning a wooded ravine.

photos.file: File:Deere & Company Headquarters, Moline, Illinois, 1956-64. Exterior - 00627v.jpg

note: Plenty of photos; also two public-domain Balthazar Korab archive images (1024px).

name: Weyerhaeuser Corporate Headquarters
by: Skidmore, Owings & Merrill (Edward Charles Bassett), with Sasaki, Walker and Associates
features: A 'skyscraper on its side': a long five-floor block with ivy on every level, between a pond and a meadow.
note: Now part of Woodbridge Corporate Park; the company left in 2016. Some files are filed under the new name.

name: Exchange House, Broadgate
features: Offices bridge the Liverpool Street railway tracks, hung from four exposed parabolic steel arches.

photos.file: File:Exchange House seen from Exchange Square.jpg
File:Exchange House in the low winter sun.jpg

name: Sainsbury Wing, National Gallery
features: Portland stone front borrows the old gallery's pilasters, then thins them out; top-lit galleries recall Soane.

photos.file: File:The National Gallery - Trafalgar Square, London - The National Gallery Sainsbury Wing (6427166221).jpg

note: The entrance was remodelled by Selldorf Architects in 2023-25; older photos show the original Venturi entrance.

name: Burton Barr Central Library
features: Copper-clad desert box; the top reading room's roof hangs on cables, and the north and south walls tune the sun.

photos.file: File:Phoenix Central Library - North East Corner - 2008-12-27.jpg

name: Monterey Bay Aquarium
features: Built on the Hovden sardine cannery site, keeping its boiler-house smokestacks; decks and tanks open onto the bay.
commons_category: Category:Exterior views of Monterey Bay Aquarium

photos.file: File:Exterior views of Monterey Bay Aquarium 2 2017-11-21.jpg

note: Use the 'Exterior views' subcategory; the main category is mostly animals and exhibits.

name: Philip Merrill Environmental Center
features: The first LEED Platinum building: a timber-framed office on the bay, using passive solar design and recycled materials.
note: Only one photo, 1024x768 (meets the 800px rule, not 1200px). It clearly shows the timber-framed building. Headquarters of the Chesapeake Bay Foundation.

name: Design Research Building
features: A shop with no solid walls: clear glass hung between thin concrete floor slabs, so the store becomes a lit display.
note: No own Commons category. Both photos show 'Architect's Corner' on Brattle Street with the glass DR building in front (Sert's office building alongside); a crop would centre it.

name: Faneuil Hall Marketplace (Quincy Market)
by: Benjamin Thompson & Associates (renovation); Alexander Parris (1826 market)
features: Three 1820s granite market halls revived as a 'festival marketplace', with glass canopies added along the sides.

photos.file: File:Dome - Quincy Market, Boston, MA - DSC05449.JPG

extras.file: File:GENERAL VIEW OF SOUTH FRONT, FROM SOUTHWEST - Quincy Market, South Market Street, Boston, Suffolk County, MA HABS MASS,13-BOST,118-8.tif

note: The award is for the 1976-78 renovation, which set the pattern for 'festival marketplaces'. The HABS file is a photo of the market (1960s-70s survey), listed here as an extra in case it's wanted; it is not a drawing.

name: The Box (Conjunctive Points)
features: A skewed box-shaped room perches on an old warehouse roof: part of Moss's remaking of the Hayden Tract.
award: AIA Twenty-five Year Award 2020 (Conjunctive Points - The New City)

photos.file: File:The Box, Eric Owen Moss, Culver City, CA (5459044960).jpg
File:The Box, Eric Owen Moss, Culver City, CA (5459045216).jpg
File:The Box, Eric Owen Moss, Culver City, CA (5459045516).jpg

note: The award covers a group of reused warehouses in Culver City's Hayden Tract (Conjunctive Points); The Box stands in for the group. Other Commons categories: Category:Stealth (building), Category:What Wall?, Category:Samitaur Tower (2010, later than the award). Don't use File:Dancing Bleachers.jpg (a different SCI-Arc installation).

name: Washington Metro stations
features: One idea repeated underground: a coffered concrete vault lit indirectly from below, with no columns on the platform.
note: The architecture here is the station interior (the vaults), so the photos are interiors by design. Opened 1976. Dupont Circle and Metro Center are typical stations.

name: Haystack Mountain School of Crafts
features: Cedar-shingled studios with peaked roofs float on piers above a steep slope, along a grand stair down to the sea.
view: side elevation across the slope: peaked-roof studios on piers stepping down beside the central stair to a landing at the water
note: No free exterior photo on Commons (the category has only two portraits; other Haystack files are interiors of an edit-a-thon). Sources confirm cedar-shingle walls and peaked roofs meeting at clean corners without overhang, buildings raised on concrete piers, linked by decks, and a grand central stair down to the water; roof pitch and window pattern are not documented, so the drawing is schematic (no windows). Four studios stand in for the 30-odd buildings.

name: History Faculty Building, Cambridge
features: An L of stepped brick-and-glass office floors wraps a fan-shaped reading room under a sloping glass roof.
award: Alvar Aalto Medal 1977 / Praemium Imperiale 1990 (James Stirling)
commons_category: Category:History Faculty Building, University of Cambridge

photos.file: File:James stirling, cambridge university history faculty building, 1964-1967 (4928152576).jpg
File:Cmglee Cambridge University Faculty of History.jpg
File:James stirling, cambridge university history faculty building, 1964-1967 (4934612209).jpg

note: Houses the Seeley Historical Library.

name: Florey Building
features: Student rooms in a red-tiled horseshoe that leans back on raking concrete legs, opening to the River Cherwell.
award: Alvar Aalto Medal 1977 / Praemium Imperiale 1990 (James Stirling)
note: Student residence for The Queen's College. SEIER+SEIER (the Flickr photographer) asks for credit if possible.

name: WZB Berlin Social Science Center
by: James Stirling, Michael Wilford and Associates
features: Offices as a cluster of archetypes (stoa, church, tower, amphitheatre) in pink and blue bands, round a garden.
award: Alvar Aalto Medal 1977 / Praemium Imperiale 1990 (James Stirling)
note: Built for IBA 1987, behind the retained 1894 Reichsversicherungsamt. File:Social Science Research Center Berlin.jpg is a street panorama mostly hidden by trees.

name: Bouça Social Housing
features: Parallel rows of stacked duplex homes with outside stairs and galleries, shielded from the railway by a long wall.
award: Alvar Aalto Medal 1988 / Praemium Imperiale 1998 (Álvaro Siza)
note: A SAAL project: first phase built 1977-78, finished in 2006, so the year is the completion. The P4230120 photo is a graffiti-covered side wall; use the 38370363485 view of the rows first. 60 files in the category.

name: Quinta da Malagueira
features: About 1,200 white courtyard row houses, served by a raised concrete 'aqueduct' carrying water and power.
award: Alvar Aalto Medal 1988 / Praemium Imperiale 1998 (Álvaro Siza)
note: Begun 1977 and built over two decades, so the year is the start. Both photos are small (1001x667 and 1024x515): above the 800px rule but not 1200px. The second shows the raised conduit. File:Evora seen from the Quinta da Malagueira... is a view of the city, not the housing.

name: Santa Maria Church, Marco de Canaveses
features: A tall white box: two towers frame a 10 m door, and a long low window lets the nave look out at sitting height.
award: Alvar Aalto Medal 1988 / Praemium Imperiale 1998 (Álvaro Siza)
commons_category: Category:Igreja de Santa Maria (Marco de Canaveses)

photos.file: File:Marco Canavezes' Church - Alvaro Siza Vieira (1933) (197037227).jpg
File:Igreja Matriz de Marco de Canaveses - Portugal (110409662).jpg

note: The two seen photos look like crops of the same view of the entrance front.

name: Simmons Hall, MIT
features: A 'sponge' dormitory: a grid of thousands of small square windows, cut through by large irregular openings.
award: Alvar Aalto Medal 1998 / Praemium Imperiale 2014 (Steven Holl)

name: Casa das Mudas Art Centre
features: Dark basalt volumes set into a cliff top above the sea, with roof terraces and paths through the building.
commons_category: Category:Centro das Artes - Casa das Mudas

photos.file: File:Madeira-Calheta-Museu de Arte Contemporânea da Madeira (modern art museum)-04ASD.jpg
File:Madeira - Casa das Mudas Arts Center, Calheta (23996208503).jpg
File:Calheta - Roof of Casa das Mudas Art Centre (24644466275).jpg

note: Now houses MUDAS, Museu de Arte Contemporânea da Madeira. Opened October 2004; largely below ground, basalt-faced. The 23996208503 photo shows the building from below, small on the cliff top.

name: Tinggården
features: Low-rise, dense housing: 78 homes in six clusters, each with its own common house; red timber walls.
note: No photo on Commons (File:KettingTinggården.JPG is a former inn in Ketting, a different place). Sources describe clusters, red-painted timber facades, yellow window frames and black timber stair towers, but not the roof shapes or the elevation, so not drawn. Vandkunsten's own project page couldn't be read from the sandbox.

name: Vanke Center (Horizontal Skyscraper)
features: A 'skyscraper lying down', as long as the Empire State is tall, raised on eight cores so the ground is a public garden.
award: Alvar Aalto Medal 1998 / Praemium Imperiale 2014 (Steven Holl)
note: No photos found on Commons (English or Chinese search). Sources give the 35 m height limit, eight cores up to 50 m apart and a perforated aluminium louvre skin, but not the clearance under the bar, storey count or how the bends read in elevation. A test elevation came out as a generic raised slab a student wouldn't recognise, so it was not kept.
